articles.title: Kling Image 4.0 on Siray AI: Native 8K, Long Pages, Sets
articles.excerpt: Kling Image 4.0, Kuaishou's newest image model, is now available on Siray AI through four API endpoints: text-to-image, edit, image sets and long pages. Prices start at $0.063 per image at 2K, and you…
articles.body: Kling Image 4.0, Kuaishou's newest image model, is now available on Siray AI through four API endpoints: text-to-image, edit, image sets and long pages. Prices start at $0.063 per image at 2K , and you can go up to native 8K. It is built for product shots, ads, storyboards and e-commerce detail pages. Key takeaways Four endpoints: text-to-image , edit (1–10 input images), image-set (1–10 outputs per request) and long-image (vertical product and web pages). Native 8K: our 8K text-to-image test came back at 7040×9344 pixels in 144 seconds and cost $0.157. Text in images: all four lines of label text in our first test came out exactly as written in the prompt. Consistent sets: a 4-image storyboard came back in 279 seconds with the same studio, wheel and bowl in every frame.
articles.author: Siray AI

Namanya Ada Lovelace, perempuan yang menulis program komputer pertama di dunia. Awalnya aku sempat mengira programmer pertama di dunia itu pasti seorang laki-laki dari era 1940-an atau 1950-an, saat komputer raksasa pertama mulai dibangun. Dugaan itu muncul karena hampir semua nama besar yang aku kenal dari sejarah komputer memang berasal dari era itu, sebut saja Alan Turing dan John von Neumann. Tapi ternyata ceritanya tidak sesederhana itu.

articles.title: Run listmonk in Docker: Self-Hosted Newsletter Manager
articles.excerpt: This tutorial was written with AI assistance from the project's official documentation. Verification status is stated at the end of the article. listmonk is a self-hosted newsletter and mailing list m…
articles.body: This tutorial was written with AI assistance from the project's official documentation. Verification status is stated at the end of the article. What listmonk does and what it needs listmonk is a self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager. It ships as a single Go binary with a Vue admin UI, backed by PostgreSQL. You get subscriber management, campaign scheduling, templates, bounce processing, and analytics without handing your list to a SaaS provider. The official Docker setup runs two containers: the listmonk/listmonk app and postgres:17-alpine . The app listens on port 9000 and talks to Postgres over a private Docker network. Uploads (media, attachments) live on disk, so you need a persistent volume or bind mount for /listmonk/uploads . The database needs its own named volume.
articles.author: konsongong

articles.title: Optimizing Web Vitals for Generative AI Widgets
articles.excerpt: Optimizing web vitals for generative AI widgets is the least glamorous work in the AI product cycle, and it decides whether the feature helps or hurts the site it lives on. The pitch is always the sam…
articles.body: Optimizing web vitals for generative AI widgets is the least glamorous work in the AI product cycle, and it decides whether the feature helps or hurts the site it lives on. The pitch is always the same: paste one script tag, get a conversational assistant. What the script tag does not say is that it will download a bundle larger than your framework, open two WebSocket connections, and hydrate a shadow DOM on the main thread while your hero image is still decoding. I have audited this pattern on enough sites now to treat it as a category rather than an incident. The widget is usually not malicious and often not badly written. It is simply built for a product demo on a fast laptop, not for a mid-range Android phone on a 4G connection opening a product page.
articles.author: Veduis

articles.title: I built a Facebook video downloader. Most people use it for the audio.
articles.excerpt: A few weeks ago I launched Facebk, a free web tool for saving public Facebook videos and Reels. I expected people to come for the videos. The data says otherwise, and it changed how I built the thing.…
articles.body: A few weeks ago I launched Facebk , a free web tool for saving public Facebook videos and Reels. I expected people to come for the videos. The data says otherwise, and it changed how I built the thing. What people actually search for In the first weeks, Google Search Console listed 205 queries that showed the site. 184 of them were about audio: "facebook to mp3", "fb video to mp3", "facebook mp3 download", plus the same idea in Arabic, Bengali and Russian. Those MP3 queries made up roughly two thirds of all impressions. The first real users I could see in the logs were Arabic speakers who pasted a Reel link and downloaded only the MP3. So the MP3 option couldn't stay a side feature. It got its own page , and the result card always shows "Audio MP3" right next to the video options.
articles.author: facebk

articles.body: SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989.
